extracted.intended_audience: registered practitioners before the USPTO (patent agents and attorneys), OED staff, and legal professionals involved in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules, procedural requirements, evidentiary burdens, and sanctioning criteria governing conduct of practitioners before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office and the discipline process (service, RFIs, defaults, and exclusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to act with reasonable diligence and promptness (37 C.F.R. §11.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example applied here: agreeing to conduct a prior art search and prepare and file a patent application but failing to do so after receiving payment; used as basis for Count I(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to keep the client reasonably informed (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must keep client reasonably informed about the status of a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner did not provide information about status and did not respond to numerous telephone calls or emails from the client (Count I(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to promptly comply with client's reasonable requests for information (37 C.F.R. §11.104(a)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must promptly comply with reasonable client requests for information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner failed to respond to repeated emails and calls requesting updates (Count I(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to promptly deliver funds the client is entitled to receive (37 C.F.R. §11.115(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must promptly deliver to the client any funds to which the client is entitled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner retained a $900 advance fee and did not refund it despite not performing services (Count I(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to refund unearned advance payments upon termination (37 C.F.R. §11.116(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must refund any advance payment of fees or expenses that has not been earned or incurred upon termination of the practitioner–client relationship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where, after termination (abandonment) of the relationship, the practitioner did not return the $900 advance fee (Count I(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation (37 C.F.R. §11.804(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit, or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where practitioner kept client funds without performing the paid-for services, characterized as dishonesty (Count I(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on acts or omissions that adversely reflect on fitness to practice (37 C.F.R. §11.804(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not engage in acts or omissions that adversely reflect on the practitioner's fitness to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied to conduct such as abandoning a client even if it may not violate a more specific misconduct provision (Count I(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to cooperate with disciplinary investigation / failure to respond to lawful demand for information (37 C.F.R. §11.801(b); 37 C.F.R. §11.22(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in an investigation and knowingly failing to respond to a lawful demand for information (RFI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where respondent signed for receipt of an RFI and then failed to respond, and/or refused or failed to accept delivery of follow-up letters (Count II(a)); the RFI was lawfully issued under 37 C.F.R. §11.22(f)(1)(ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. §11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioner must not engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied where failure to respond to OED's RFI or letters impeded the disciplinary process (Count II(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to notify OED Director of change of postal address (37 C.F.R. §11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered practitioners must provide written notice to the OED Director of any change in their postal address within thirty days of the change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to update address can result in returned mail and service by publication; was a factual basis for service issues in this case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication when service copy is returned (37 C.F.R. §11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If mailed service is returned, the Office may serve by publishing notice in two consecutive issues of the USPTO Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used here after certified mail to the practitioner's address was returned; publication dates and instruction on obtaining a copy of the complaint are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to answer complaint: admission/default (37 C.F.R. §11.36(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file an answer will constitute an admission of the allegations in the complaint and may result in entry of default judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent's failure to answer led to being deemed to have admitted allegations and to the Court entering default judgment; findings of fact are treated as admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof: clear and convincing evidence (37 C.F.R. §11.49)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director has the burden of proving alleged violations by clear and convincing evidence; respondent must prove any affirmative defense by clear and convincing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard governing evidentiary burden in disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — violation of duty owed (37 C.F.R. §11.54(b) factor 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the practitioner has violated a duty owed to the client, to the public, to the legal system, or to the profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First of four factors the Tribunal must consider before imposing sanctions; applied here to assess seriousness of abandoning client and keeping unearned fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — practitioner's state of mind (37 C.F.R. §11.54(b) factor 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the practitioner acted intentionally, knowingly, or negligently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second sanction factor used to gauge culpability (case finds respondent acted intentionally/knowingly).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — amount of actual or potential injury (37 C.F.R. §11.54(b) factor 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of the actual or potential injury caused by the practitioner's misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third sanction factor; here, client suffered delay in patent filing and loss of $900.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning factor — aggravating and mitigating factors (37 C.F.R. §11.54(b) factor 4; ABA Standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence of any aggravating or mitigating factors when assessing an appropriate sanction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tribunal may reference ABA Standards for Imposing Lawyer Sanctions. Aggravating factors applied here include: bad faith obstruction of the proceeding by failing to comply (Standards §9.22(e)); dishonest or selfish motive (Standards §9.22(b)); indifference to making restitution (cited as Standards §9.220 in the decision); failure to acknowledge wrongdoing or show remorse. Mitigation noted: lack of prior disciplinary record (Standards §9.32(a)), but may be outweighed by aggravation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Available sanction: exclusion from practice and reinstatement conditions (37 C.F.R. §11.60(b); §11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO is an available sanction; excluded practitioners are eligible to apply for reinstatement no earlier than five years after the effective date of exclusion; reinstatement may be conditioned (e.g., restitution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision ordered exclusion from practice in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters; directs respondent to 37 C.F.R. §11.58 for responsibilities in cases of suspension/exclusion and references that reinstatement may be conditioned on restitution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribunal jurisdiction and authority to suspend/exclude (35 U.S.C. §32; 37 C.F.R. §§11.19, 11.32, 11.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO has exclusive authority to establish qualifications for admission to practice before it and to suspend or exclude persons from practice; the Tribunal has jurisdiction over the proceeding under statutory and regulatory provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited statutory/regulatory basis for discipline; informs that sanctions such as suspension/exclusion are within USPTO's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for Requests for Information (RFI) lawfully issued (37 C.F.R. §11.22(f)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: OED may lawfully issue a Request for Information and Evidence under 37 C.F.R. §11.22(f); the RFI sets a response deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used here where the First RFI was issued, delivered and signed for on a known date and requested response within thirty days; failure to respond is actionable under the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights after initial decision (37 C.F.R. §11.55(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty days of the initial decision, either party may file an appeal to the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural right noted in the decision; standard timeline for appellate review of disciplinary decisions.
